# Ambient audio

How catLock's six ambient loops are made, why they sound the way they do, and what to check before shipping.

---

## Provenance — the short version

**Every loop is generated by `scripts/synth_audio.py`.** Nothing is downloaded, sampled or licensed. There is no attribution to track, no CC-BY-NC trap, no third-party licence that can be revoked, and nothing to add to `legal/ASSET_LICENCES.md` beyond "generated in-house".

This was a deliberate choice over sourcing free audio from Freesound or Pixabay. The trade: café and purr are not in the set, because neither can be synthesised convincingly. Café needs real voices and clatter; a synthetic purr lands in uncanny-valley territory, which is the worst possible outcome for an app whose identity is a cat. If those are wanted later, source them as **CC0** and record the licence.

## The six sounds

| Sound | How it's built | Free / Plus |
|---|---|---|
| Rain | Pink noise band-passed 300 Hz–9 kHz, plus ~5,200 sparse droplet transients | Free |
| Ocean | 1/f^1.7 noise, low-passed at 1.6 kHz, under a three-layer swell | Free |
| Fireplace | Warm low-passed bed plus ~900 sharp crackles at 1.2–6.5 kHz | Plus |
| White noise | Flat spectrum, gently rolled off above 15 kHz | Free |
| Pink noise | 1/f | Plus |
| Brown noise | 1/f^1.6, high-passed at 40 Hz | Plus |

**Format:** mono AAC in `.m4a`, 44.1 kHz, 96 kbps, 60 seconds. Roughly 720 KB each, **4.5 MB total.**

Mono is deliberate — it halves the size, and none of these sounds carry meaningful stereo information.

## Why they loop without a click

The naive approach is to crossfade the tail into the head. That was tried first and the seam was measurable on three of six files.

The technique used instead: **every sound is synthesised in the frequency domain over exactly N samples.** An inverse FFT of length N is periodic with period N by construction, so sample N wraps to sample 0 with no discontinuity at all — no crossfade, no fade-in, no seam. Two consequences to preserve if you regenerate:

- Time-domain events (raindrops, crackles) are **wrapped modulo N**, so one landing near the end continues at the start.
- The ocean's swell LFOs use frequencies of `k / 60 Hz` — an integer number of cycles per loop. A 0.085 Hz LFO would not close.

Verified by comparing the wrap-point sample delta against the mean sample-to-sample delta. All six are at or below 1.15×, i.e. indistinguishable from ordinary signal movement.

## Level matching, and why it isn't perfect

Five of six sit at **−23 LUFS**. Fireplace lands at about −27 because its crackle transients hit the peak ceiling first; it gets a `gainTrim` of 1.5 in `SoundOption` instead of being re-rendered with the crackles squashed.

Two things learned the hard way here, worth not rediscovering:

- **LUFS is a poor yardstick for noise colours.** K-weighting heavily discounts bass, so a true −6 dB/octave brown noise measured −44 LUFS at full scale. Forcing it to −23 demanded ~20 dB of gain, which clipped and then got mangled by the limiter. The fix was musical, not technical: slope 1.6 instead of 2.0, high-passed at 40 Hz. Still unmistakably brown, but the energy sits where ears are rather than in inaudible rumble.
- **`gainTrim` exists because loudness matching for noise is ultimately a judgement call.** The values in `SoundOption` are starting points measured by meter, not by ear. **Tune them on a real device, in a quiet room, at low volume**, and commit the result.

## Which sound plays, and when

There is **always** a selected sound — Rain by default — so a session never
starts silent by accident. `HomeViewModel` restores the choice from
`UserPreferences.selectedSoundID` on launch and writes it back on every change;
before this it was never read or written, so the choice was lost on every
relaunch.

Silence is a deliberate choice, not an accident: the Sounds sheet has an
**Ambient sound** toggle backed by `soundEnabled`. When it is off,
`sessionSound` is nil and `FocusSessionViewModel.start()` calls `stop()` —
which matters, because otherwise a preview still running from the sheet would
carry straight into a session the user chose to run in silence.

A stored ID from a build that had `purr` or `cafe` falls back to Rain via
`SoundOption.option(id:)` rather than leaving the user with nothing.

## Audio session behaviour — read this before shipping

`AudioPlayerService` uses **`.ambient` with `.mixWithOthers`**:

- ✅ Mixes with Spotify, podcasts, anything already playing
- ✅ Honours the physical silent switch
- ❌ **Stops when the app is backgrounded or the screen locks**

That last one matters for a focus timer, where putting the phone face-down is the entire point. iOS does not offer a category that both respects the silent switch and survives backgrounding — the two behaviours are tied together.

**To switch:** change the category to `.playback` in `activateSessionIfNeeded()` and add `UIBackgroundModes: [audio]` to Info.plist. Sound then survives the lock screen, but a muted phone will still make noise. Apple does check at review that an app declaring the background audio mode genuinely needs it; a focus timer playing continuous ambience qualifies.

This is an open decision — see `DECISIONS.md`.

## Regenerating

```bash
python3 scripts/synth_audio.py            # writes WAVs
python3 scripts/synth_audio.py --encode   # normalise + encode to .m4a
```

Requires `numpy` and `ffmpeg`. The random seed is fixed at 7, so output is reproducible — change the seed for different rain.

## Testing checklist

**Route audit** — `python3 scripts/audit_routes.py` checks unreachable screens, sheets with no way out, presentation flags that are never raised, missing imports, and every `SoundOption` resolving to a bundled file. It exits non-zero, so CI can gate on it. This is the closest thing to clicking every button that is available without a Swift toolchain.

**Automated** (`goCatTests/SoundAssetTests.swift`) — every `SoundOption` has a bundled file, every file decodes, is longer than 30s and is mono, `gainTrim` values are sane, and toggling the same sound twice stops it. These exist because the old `AudioPlayerServiceTests` asserted that a Bool flipped and stayed green for weeks while the folder was empty.

**Manual, on a real device — none of this can be automated:**

- [ ] Listen to each sound for a full 90 seconds. **You are listening for the loop point at 0:60.** If you can hear where it wraps, the file is broken.
- [ ] Switch between all six at a fixed volume. Does any one jump out? Adjust its `gainTrim`.
- [ ] Play at the lowest non-zero volume — noise reveals encoding artefacts most at low level.
- [ ] Wired headphones, Bluetooth headphones, and the speaker. Bluetooth codecs treat noise unkindly.
- [ ] Start Spotify, then start a sound. Both should play.
- [ ] Flip the silent switch. Sound should stop.
- [ ] Lock the screen. **Sound will stop** — confirm that is the behaviour you want.
- [ ] Take a phone call mid-session, then hang up. Sound must resume by itself; if it doesn't, the interruption handler is broken.
- [ ] Unplug headphones mid-playback.
- [ ] Leave one running for a full 45-minute session and check battery and thermals.
